outputs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Produce FOUR full-body original painted Kilnward Mallet battle sprites in a TWO by TWO sheet on flat vivid chroma green #00ff00, no green spill or floor shadows. Images 1 and 2 are motion guides ONLY for the top-left and top-right figures respectively; Image 3 is authoritative character, materials, gear, camera and rendering reference. Do not reproduce the diagrams, colors or text. Preserve broad muscular middle-aged bearded smith, tied dark hair and headband, black rolled sleeves, brown riveted leather apron/pauldrons/bracers, red brick kiln-arch motif, dark reinforced boots. Exactly ONE rectangular iron mallet on a long wooden handle, exactly TWO natural hands gripping its shaft in every pose.
TOP LEFT: use Image 1 leg geometry: NEAR leg straight planted under hip, FAR knee swings forward with far boot lifted behind near shin; hips above planted near boot. Both hands carry mallet across waist, head to RIGHT.
TOP RIGHT: use Image 2 leg geometry, not Image 1: FAR leg straight planted, NEAR thigh raised diagonally forward to RIGHT and NEAR knee bent, near boot suspended in front of far shin; hips above far support foot. Raised near thigh visibly overlaps far thigh. Same face/camera/torso/weapon, do not mirror torso. This must be an opposite support phase, not a copy or different camera.
BOTTOM LEFT: recovery after downward forward mallet slam, feet grounded, torso still forward while both hands draw low mallet upward toward waist, head low on RIGHT. Elbows bent and shaft continuous.
BOTTOM RIGHT: guard release, planted feet, torso straightening, mallet held diagonal across chest with both hands, less compressed than a deep block.
Match reference painterly small-scale game art, body/head/hammer size across all four frames. Full soles, hair and mallet tip within each cell and generous gutters. No effects, motion streaks, new gear, text, checkerboard or background.
outputs.selection_notes: 15 packed frames select 11 original RGBA paintings and four new supported passing, low two-handed mallet recovery and guard-release paintings. Original overhead windup, low strike, crouched guard, recoil, buckle, side fall and head-right resting corpse remain; duplicate original contact is unselected. Original genuine alpha reused; new green-backed source prepared with approved bounded edge cleanup. Uniform per-source scales 0.60/0.36, support anchors and inspected banded boundaries preserve the mallet and falling boot without the neighboring hammer fragment. Separate passing guides do not establish alternating near/far support: the generated poses still appear to lift the same leg through backward/forward positions. Full gait, hammer/hand/shoulder continuity, palette/edges, grounding and connected recovery/death timing remain refinement; not final accepted animation.
